kind.label: Kinds of confref datasets
kind.definition: What a dataset is: its role in the confref knowledge graph.

records.label: Records
records.definition: Records from one source about conference series, events, proceedings or other entities, one resource per record.

authority.label: Authority data
authority.definition: Records of an authority file selected because our datasets name them (e.g. the GND), kept as the source states them: reference points and evidence for links, not a source of series and events of its own. A source taken as a whole for its series and events (dblp, Wikidata, ConfIDent) is records.

complement.label: Complement
complement.definition: Statements about the resources of other datasets that only add to them (normalised values, enrichments, links), without changing them.

linkset.label: Linkset
linkset.definition: Links between resources of different datasets, or from them to resources outside confref, and nothing else.

correction.label: Correction
correction.definition: Corrections of the data of other datasets: triples it adds (its data) and triples it deletes from every graph that contains them (a SPARQL Update file); applied after all other datasets.

entity-pages.label: Identifier set
entity-pages.definition: The confref identifiers: one resource per entity (conference series, event), bringing together the records about it.

ontology.label: Ontology
ontology.definition: Classes and properties used to describe the data.

vocabulary.label: Vocabulary
vocabulary.definition: A controlled vocabulary: concepts used as values in the data or in its description.

support.label: Support data
support.definition: Data that other datasets are made from or that describes them (caches, label lists, page metadata, agents), rather than data about the entities themselves.

method.label: Methods by which confref datasets are made
method.definition: How the statements of a dataset were made; a dataset may name several methods.

automated.label: Automated
automated.definition: Made automatically by a method whose statements can be wrong individually, and not checked statement by statement by people (at most samples were checked).

curated.label: Curated
curated.definition: Made or checked statement by statement by people.

scraped.label: Scraped
scraped.definition: Extracted from web pages written for human readers.

converted.label: Converted
converted.definition: Converted by a program from structured data of the source (an export, a dump, an API), keeping its content.

deterministic.label: Deterministic
deterministic.definition: Derived by a program from other data with exact rules: the same input always gives the same statements, and every statement follows from the input.

rule-based.label: Rule-based
rule-based.definition: Derived with heuristic rules: patterns, normalisation, and matching by names, labels or similarity (also when looking up a name in an external service); a statement can be wrong in an individual case.

lookup.label: Lookup
lookup.definition: Looked up by identifier in an external service (e.g. a GND number in DNB EntityFacts, a Wikidata item); taken as correct. Matching by names is rule-based.

statistical.label: Statistical
statistical.definition: Made by statistical methods or machine learning (scores, estimates, automatic entity linking); statements are probable, not certain.

machine-translation.label: Machine translation
machine-translation.definition: Translated automatically by a machine translation service (e.g. Google Translate); translations may be wrong.

llm-judged.label: LLM-judged
llm-judged.definition: Selected or checked statement by statement by a large language model that judged each one on the evidence shown (e.g. which links of a source are correct); the judgements can be wrong and were not checked by people.

ai-generated.label: AI-generated
ai-generated.definition: Made by generative AI (large language models); statements may be wrong and were not checked one by one.
